title: Precision Pinbook: sampled publish & pin workflow for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and ship a lightweight, auditable 'Precision Pinbook' publish workflow that produces Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, normalized cost) for model variants and pins a canonical runtime mapping. The workflow must support sampled production shadowing, variant cost normalization (quantized vs fp16), signed artifacts, staged publish with automated rollback signals, and easy operator reconciliation.
background: We already produce verified profiles but current publish flow is heavy (full-batch benchmarks) and brittle when serving variants (quantized, sparsified). Teams request faster onboarding, smaller sample footprints, and clearer cost-normalization so product teams can pin model versions confidently without long benchmarking cycles. This initiative aims to reduce time-to-verify and decrease manual overhead while preserving signal quality for latency and cost SLAs.
tasks: Define sampling strategy for production shadowing and synthetic microbench mix
Create cost-normalization formula to translate sampled latency/throughput into per-token cost across variants
Design signed profile artifact schema (metadata, perf vectors, hash, provenance) and storage location
Implement publish pipeline: staging -> sampled shadow -> canary -> publish -> auto-rollback hooks
Add console UI for Pinbook entries: lineage, pinned runtime, sample windows, and rollback history
Integrate verification checklist into model onboarding playbook and template PRs
Add telemetry contracts (required histograms/percentiles) and alert thresholds for publish failures
acceptance_criteria: Profile publish pipeline can run with a 10% production traffic shadow sample for a new model variant and produce a signed profile artifact under 3 hours
Cost-normalization gives <5% deviation vs full-bench reference on 3 benchmarked models (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, sparse)
Console shows a Pinbook entry with pin metadata, sampled window, canary rollout status, and rollback affordance
Automated rollback triggers on two consecutive 99th percentile latency regressions above configured threshold
Audit trail stored for every publish including signer, input commit, sampled traces link, and signed hash
decisions: Adopt a hybrid sampling approach: short synthetic microbench to capture kernel performance + 10% shadow of real traffic for KV/prefix behavior
Signed artifacts will be JSONL with a canonical field order and SHA-256 signature; signatures recorded in a minimal ledger S3 path
Normalization baseline is fp16 on A100 with sequence length 256; variants receive multiplicative adjustments derived from sampled microbench ratios
Use existing canary-as-code infra for rollout steps and integrate with runtime-1.21 release gates
risks: Sampling may miss rare tail behaviors leading to false-positive publishes; mitigated by requiring two independent sample windows
Normalization model could under/over-correct cost for highly sparse or structured models; mitigation: safety multiplier and manual review for outliers
Sign-off latency: stakeholders may delay pin approvals; mitigation: pre-authorized steward list for low-risk, re-verifiable profiles
Storage and privacy concerns for sampled traces; only store redacted traces and aggregate histograms in the artifact
